editorialStatus: Source-transcribed pathways; suggested documentation is not an insurer-provided checklist

guides.heading: Step therapy and clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The statewide drug list says step through metformin. The detailed guideline supplies indication-specific routes, including heart failure and CKD routes without a metformin trial requirement.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes
all: Patient is at least 10 years old.
Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
History of metformin failure at a minimum 1,500 mg daily for 90 days, OR contraindication, OR intolerance to metformin.

pathways.title: Adult type 2 diabetes with established cardiovascular disease
all: Medication is requested to reduce cardiovascular death risk in an adult with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
History of metformin failure at a minimum 1,500 mg daily for 90 days, OR contraindication, OR intolerance to metformin.

pathways.title: Adult heart failure OR adult CKD at risk of progression
all: Medication is requested to reduce cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in an adult with heart failure; OR to reduce eGFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization in an adult with CKD at risk of progression.
No metformin trial is specified for this qualifying guideline pathway.

documentationSuggestions: Record the indication and supporting diagnosis.
For a metformin-dependent pathway, document the dose, dates, duration and response; alternatively document the specific contraindication or intolerance.
For the heart failure or CKD pathway, document the qualifying condition and clinical rationale.
guides.guidelineCaution: The statewide drug list flags step therapy rather than an explicit general PA requirement. The separate statewide clinical guideline is titled Prior Authorization; the plan determines the actual claim and authorization workflow.
sourceChecks: Requested medication is being used for one of the following

guides.heading: Prior authorization clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The guideline permits either the specified prior-insulin pathway OR a clinical reason the patient needs concentrated insulin.

pathways.title: Prior insulin failure, intolerance or contraindication
all: History of failure, intolerance, or contraindication to insulin aspart OR insulin lispro.
History of failure, intolerance, or contraindication to Lantus.

pathways.title: Clinical need for concentrated insulin
all: There is a reason or special circumstance that the patient needs a concentrated insulin product.

documentationSuggestions: For the prior-insulin pathway, record which rapid-acting insulin and Lantus were tried, treatment outcomes, or the reason each cannot be used.
For the concentrated-insulin pathway, document the patient-specific reason a concentrated insulin formulation is needed.
guides.guidelineCaution: The guideline does not specify a universal insulin-dose threshold or an additional required laboratory test. Do not infer one.
sourceChecks: Humulin R U-500 vial and kwikpen

guides.heading: Mounjaro prior authorization clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The November 2026 AHCCCS GLP-1 guideline specifies the following requirements for Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes. All criteria apply.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes — all requirements
all: Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus documented in submitted medical records.
Baseline hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5%; the laboratory report MUST be submitted.
Either: paid claims verifying metformin failure at ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days; OR documented metformin contraindication or intolerance.
Patient is at least 10 years old.
Medication is not being used for weight loss.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR provides a plan to address concomitant use.
Medication is not being co-administered with another GLP-1 receptor agonist.

documentationSuggestions: Submit a baseline A1c laboratory report showing ≥6.5%, plus chart records confirming type 2 diabetes.

For metformin treatment failure, verify ≥1,500 mg/day for 90 days through paid pharmacy claims (the guideline explicitly requires paid-claim verification); otherwise document contraindication or intolerance.
Document the intended indication and review concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor and GLP-1 receptor agonist use.
guides.guidelineCaution: This guideline is for type 2 diabetes; the source states weight-loss/appetite-suppression requests are plan exclusions. Its 'Preferred Drugs' section names Mounjaro, but that heading does not override the separate current statewide drug-list preference field or establish a particular plan's benefit.
sourceChecks: Preferred Drugs: Mounjaro, Trulicity, Brand Victoza
Baseline A1C greater than or equal to 6.5%

guides.heading: Farxiga clinical authorization qualifications
guides.summary: The AHCCCS November 2026 SGLT-2 guideline lists two alternative qualification pathways for brand Farxiga. Either indication pathway qualifies under the stated guideline.

pathways.title: Type 2 diabetes
all: Patient is at least 10 years old.
Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
History of metformin failure at a minimum 1,500 mg/day for 90 days, OR contraindication, OR intolerance to metformin.

pathways.title: CKD or qualifying heart failure
all: ONE of: chronic kidney disease (CKD); OR heart failure NYHA class II–IV with reduced ejection fraction; OR heart failure NYHA class II–IV with preserved ejection fraction.
No metformin trial is specified for this CKD/heart-failure qualification pathway.

documentationSuggestions: For type 2 diabetes, document patient age, diabetes diagnosis, and metformin trial dose/duration/outcome or contraindication/intolerance.
For CKD or heart failure, document the qualifying diagnosis and, for heart failure, NYHA functional class and ejection-fraction category.
guides.guidelineCaution: This guide applies only to brand Farxiga. Generic dapagliflozin requests have an additional explicit prerequisite: failure, intolerance, or contraindication to brand Farxiga. That extra generic-only rule is not applied to the brand product.

guides.heading: Awiqli initial and renewal PA qualifications
guides.summary: Awiqli initial approval and renewal have different requirements. Select the applicable treatment stage; do not treat renewal criteria as an alternative pathway for first-time initiation.

stages.title: Initial authorization
all: Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient is at least 18 years old.
Inadequate glycemic control on non-insulin antidiabetic therapy (HbA1c ≥7%).

any: Trial and inadequate response to TWO of Lantus (insulin glargine), Rezvoglar KwikPen (insulin glargine), or Tresiba (insulin degludec), with at least a 90-day supply; OR contraindications to TWO of these basal insulins.

Submitted documentation demonstrates a barrier to safe self-administration of daily insulin (examples in the source include daily-basal nonadherence, visual impairment, caregiver assistance, physical or cognitive limitations).

all: Patient or caregiver counseled on weekly dosing, hypoglycemia risk/recognition/management, and avoidance of concurrent basal insulin.

stages.title: Reauthorization
all: Positive clinical response to treatment (for example, decreased HbA1c from baseline).

documentationSuggestions: For initiation, document T2DM, age, A1c and lack of glycemic control on non-insulin treatment.
Provide claims or chart records of the required two basal-insulin failures/contraindications, or document the safety barrier to daily insulin.
Record counseling and avoid overlapping basal insulin. For renewal document response since baseline.
guides.guidelineCaution: The Awiqli initial/renewal distinction is explicit in the published policy. The source does not state a specific universal insulin-dose threshold.

guides.heading: Soliqua initial and renewal PA qualifications
guides.summary: Soliqua requires type 2 diabetes and inadequate control with both a GLP-1 receptor agonist and basal insulin for initial authorization; renewal criteria are different.

stages.title: Initial authorization
all: Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Inadequate glycemic control on BOTH a GLP-1 receptor agonist and a basal insulin.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR has developed a plan to address concomitant use.

stages.title: Reauthorization
all: Documentation of a positive clinical response to therapy.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR has developed a plan to address concomitant use.

documentationSuggestions: Document T2DM and inadequate control with prior GLP-1 receptor agonist plus basal insulin treatment.
Document the DPP-4 inhibitor medication review or plan. For renewal document clinical response.
guides.guidelineCaution: Source examples of GLP-1 receptor agonists and basal insulins are illustrative, not an additional requirement to try every listed agent.
sourceChecks: Inadequately controlled on BOTH of the following

stages.title: Reauthorization
all: Documentation of a positive clinical response to therapy.
Provider attests no concurrent DPP-4 inhibitor-containing drug, OR has developed a plan to address concomitant use.

guides.heading: Vitamin D initial and renewal clinical qualifications
guides.summary: The AHCCCS guideline requires laboratory documentation of Vitamin D deficiency for initial authorization and documentation of improvement for renewal. The criteria are indication-specific.

stages.title: Initial authorization
all: Submit medical records (e.g., chart notes) including laboratory values documenting Vitamin D deficiency.

stages.title: Reauthorization
all: Submit medical records (e.g., chart notes) including laboratory values documenting improvement in Vitamin D deficiency (e.g., levels within normal range).

documentationSuggestions: Provide the relevant Vitamin D laboratory result and chart documentation supporting deficiency for initial review; provide follow-up laboratory values demonstrating improvement for renewal.
guides.guidelineCaution: These criteria are taken from the named vitamin policy. The policy index alone does not establish that every vitamin product/formulation requires PA.

guides.heading: Recorlev initial and reauthorization criteria
guides.summary: The source contains separate Cushing’s disease and NCCN-supported regimen pathways, each with distinct initial and renewal requirements.

stages.title: Initial authorization — Cushing’s disease
all: Diagnosis of Cushing’s disease.

any: Patient is not a candidate for pituitary surgery.
Pituitary surgery has not been curative.

stages.title: Reauthorization — Cushing’s disease
all: Documentation of positive response to therapy.

stages.title: Initial authorization — NCCN recommended regimen
all: Requested use is supported by the NCCN Drugs and Biologics Compendium with Category of Evidence and Consensus 1, 2A, or 2B.

stages.title: Reauthorization — NCCN recommended regimen
all: Documentation of positive clinical response to therapy.

documentationSuggestions: For Cushing’s disease, document diagnosis and surgical ineligibility or lack of cure following surgery.
For NCCN-supported use, identify the relevant compendium regimen and evidence category.
For renewal, document positive response to therapy.
guides.guidelineCaution: The NCCN route and Cushing’s disease route are separate indication-specific pathways; renewal is not an initial-approval alternative. This statewide guideline does not itself establish coverage under an individual plan.

guides.heading: Rezurock PA and BID quantity-limit criteria
guides.summary: Initial chronic graft-versus-host disease approval requires prior systemic therapy and a qualifying specialist. Renewal requires no evidence of progression. The separate twice-daily quantity-limit pathway is contingent on a CYP3A inducer or proton pump inhibitor.

stages.title: Initial authorization — chronic graft-versus-host disease
all: Diagnosis of chronic graft-versus-host disease.
Trial and failure of two or more lines of systemic therapy.

any: Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist.
Prescribed by or in consultation with an oncologist.
Prescribed by or in consultation with a physician experienced in transplant-patient management.

stages.title: Reauthorization — chronic graft-versus-host disease
all: Patient does not show evidence of progressive disease while on therapy.

documentationSuggestions: For initiation, document cGVHD, two prior systemic therapy lines and specialist involvement.
For renewal, document absence of disease progression.
For twice-daily use, document the concomitant strong CYP3A inducer or proton pump inhibitor.
guides.guidelineCaution: The twice-daily branch is a separate quantity-limit criterion, not a general requirement for standard once-daily authorization. Individual-plan coverage remains separate.

guides.heading: Kimmtrak initial and renewal PA
guides.summary: Initial approval requires unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma, HLA-A*02:01 positivity by high-resolution genotyping, and oncology involvement. Renewal requires evidence of no progression.

stages.title: Initial authorization
all: Medical records document uveal melanoma.
Disease is unresectable or metastatic.
Patient is HLA-A*02:01 genotype positive by a high-resolution genotyping test.
Prescribed by or in consultation with an oncologist.

stages.title: Reauthorization
all: Medical records document no evidence of progressive disease while on therapy.

documentationSuggestions: Submit melanoma diagnosis, disease stage, HLA-A*02:01 high-resolution genotype and oncologist involvement.
For renewal submit response/progression documentation.
guides.guidelineCaution: Initial and renewal criteria are distinct; renewal alone does not qualify initial therapy. Plan-specific benefit remains unverified by this statewide policy.
